About.tagline: Storyteller. Historian. Your personal window into Austin.
About.bio1: Hi! I'm Tatiana Orlova — a passionate storyteller, history enthusiast, and your personal guide to Austin, Texas.
About.bio2: I first arrived in Austin over a decade ago, falling head over heels for a city that somehow manages to be everything at once: funky and historic, laid-back and electric, Southern and thoroughly its own. What started as a personal love affair with Austin's neighborhoods, hidden courtyards, and eccentric legends slowly turned into a calling. I realized that the stories I discovered while wandering the city — about outlaws and opera houses, literary giants and ghost-ridden saloons — were too good to keep to myself. That's when Austin City Tours was born.
About.bio3: I believe the best way to know a city is through its stories. Dates and facts are easy to forget; a gripping tale about O. Henry — the beloved short-story writer who found his voice in an Austin jail cell — stays with you forever. Every tour I lead is built around narrative. We visit places that shaped Austin's identity and I bring them to life with the characters, conflicts, and coincidences that made the city what it is today.
About.bio4: I design my tours to be conversations, not lectures. Whether we're tracing the elegant Victorian mansions of the Bremond Block, exploring the literary legacy of William Sidney Porter in Hyde Park, or stepping inside the Texas State Capitol, I encourage questions, detours, and moments of genuine discovery. No two tours are ever exactly the same.
About.bio5: I'm originally from Russia, and I have a special place in my heart for Austin's Russian-speaking community. Many of my tours are conducted in Russian, giving newcomers and visitors a warm, familiar way to explore their adopted city. Connecting people to Austin in their native language — seeing that moment when the city stops feeling foreign and starts feeling like home — is one of the most rewarding parts of my work. That said, all tours are equally available in English, and I welcome guests from every background.
About.bio6: Austin rewards curiosity. The more you look, the more you find: a hidden courtyard behind a 19th-century storefront, a mosaic-tiled alley connecting two eras, a neighborhood that survived a century of change with its soul intact. I find something new every single time I walk these streets, and that sense of discovery is exactly what I want every guest to feel. I'm also deeply committed to accuracy — I read, I research, I visit archives. When I tell you that the Chateau Bellevue was once Austin's premier social club, or that the ghosts said to haunt certain downtown blocks have stories rooted in real history, I back it up.
About.bio7: Whether you're a first-time visitor trying to understand what makes Austin tick, a long-time resident ready to see your city with fresh eyes, or a Russian speaker looking for a familiar voice in an unfamiliar place — I'd love to guide you. Austin has given me so much. Every tour is my way of giving a little of that back.
